newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton falls ahead of Cotton Board meet.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton falls ahead of Cotton Board meet.

text.p: Indian cotton prices fell on Friday ahead of a meeting on Monday of the Cotton Advisory Board which usually discusses output and demand trends, dealers said.
Fresh mill buying was low while slow overseas buying dragged down prices on light profit-taking.
The Cotton Advisory Board meeting, convened by the Textile Commissioner, is expected to review production and demand trends as was the case at previous meetings, traders said.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by five rupees at 780/820 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned fell by 5/10 rupees to 1,400/1,625 rupees per maund. F-414 fell by 20/25 rupees to 1,830/1,845 rupees per maund.

Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) was quiet at 11,400/11,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while about 400/500 rupees bales (170 kg each) of the Gujarat Sankar-4 cotton changed hands at the steady level of 17,700/18,500 rupees per candy.
